subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fastcommerce.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@fastcommerce.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Quick sync — streaming demo today

Thanks for the demo earlier — that was helpful. A quick recap on our end and a couple of clarifying questions before we put together a mutual action plan:

- Goal: replace our home page personalization microservice with an LLM-based reranker + short-form generation. Typical request: 1-3 prompts, expected output 40-120 tokens.
- Traffic profile: peak ~120 req/s, sustained 60 req/s; 95th percentile concurrency target ~80 concurrent requests.
- Latency SLOs: we need time-to-first-token (TTFT) <= 120ms p95; end-to-end (first byte to last byte) p95 <= 400ms for short responses.
- Streaming: prefer SSE or WebSocket for partial tokens. We need chunks delivered every ~150-300ms to make UI feel snappy; if that's not feasible, 1-2 chunk cadence per response is acceptable.

Questions:
1) Do you have prior examples of achieving TTFT p95 ~100-120ms on similar models with our request sizes?
2) For concurrency 80 and peak 120 req/s, would we need Dedicated capacity or can hosted autoscale meet this with predictable p95 latency?

I'll attach our internal SLO doc — happy to jump on a follow-up call.

Thanks,
Alex
Director, Platform Engineering
FastCommerce

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@fastcommerce.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear recap and for sharing the SLO doc. Quick answers and proposed next steps below.

Short answers to your questions:
- Yes — we've hit TTFT p95 in the ~70-130ms range on short responses for similar workloads by using a combination of prefix/KV caching, continuous batching with small max batch sizes, and choosing lower-latency model variants (8-bit quantized). We can share benchmark artifacts.
- For predictable p95 at 80 concurrent targets, Dedicated is recommended if you require strict SLAs and cost predictability. Hosted can often meet these numbers in many regions under normal load, but bursts and noisy neighbors can affect p95 unless you provision Dedicated or set routing to higher-performance tiers.

Streaming specifics:
- We support SSE and WebSocket streaming. Typical chunk cadence we’ve seen is 100-250ms per chunk for short outputs when using our optimized runtime and small token emission sizes.
- We can tune chunk size vs cadence: e.g., 1-2 tokens per chunk at ~120ms cadence or 5-10 tokens per chunk at ~250ms cadence depending on UX preference.

Proposed next steps:
1) We'll run a focused benchmark: TTFT p95, p99, and chunk cadence under your payload (40-120 tokens) at 60 sustained / 120 peak req/s and 80 concurrency.
2) Provide recommended deployment: Hosted high-tier vs Dedicated sizing (GPU type, pool size) and an estimated monthly cost.
3) Share a short write-up on streaming tradeoffs (SSE vs WS), chunk cadence options, and UX recommendations for FastCommerce.

Can you confirm a 2-hour window next week for a short load-test kickoff? Also confirming you can share a representative request/response pair and the demo recording for context.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — internal note + plan

Marissa — quick internal note before the kickoff. Observations and actions: 

- Target TTFT p95 <= 120ms with concurrency 80 + peak 120 req/s is achievable on a Dedicated pool using A10G/A100p-like GPUs with:
  * Continuous batching configured with max_batch_size 16 and batch latency target 10-20ms.
  * Prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts (we saw ~30-50% TTFT improvement for similar ecom rerank workloads).
  * 8-bit quantized model variant (we should validate quality impact).

- Streaming cadence: recommend starting with ~150ms cadence and 3-5 token chunks; will measure UX tradeoffs during load test.

Action items for kickoff (Thu 2026-12-08):
1) Run bench harness at 60/120 req/s with 80 concurrency; capture TTFT p50/p95/p99 and chunk inter-arrival distribution. (Owner: Dylan)
2) Validate hosted vs dedicated latency profiles (quick side-by-side synthetic test). (Owner: Vivek)
3) Provide Dedicated sizing + cost estimate and a short doc on streaming cadence UX. (Owner: Marissa)

I'll prep the harness and a short script to reproduce the results. Marissa — can you confirm you own the cost estimate doc? Dylan — please sync with Priya for the sample payload format.

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
